source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS01 publishes 114 MW of IT capacity across 685,000 square feet in Sterling, Virginia, making it the third-largest disclosed data center in the state.

Virginia has 25 facilities that publish megawatt figures, totaling 1,603 MW. Ashburn AS01 alone accounts for 7.1 percent of that published load. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 114 MW implies roughly 2,850 racks, though the operator does not state workload mix or tenant configuration. The state maps 330 facilities, so the great majority disclose no capacity at all and cannot be ranked or summed.

For AI specifically, the number that matters is the megawatt figure, because accelerators are power-limited before they are space-limited. A campus of this size is a consequential draw on whatever serves it. But the data stops at the fence line. It does not say whether the 114 MW comes from existing utility supply or new generation, where the facility interconnects, or whether the full capacity is allocated or available. LEED certification speaks to building efficiency, not to power source or grid characteristics.

What the data does establish is scale and position within disclosed Virginia capacity. What it cannot establish is whether this campus relieves or tightens the state's power constraint, because the supply side is simply not published.
